news.headline: Young finished Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons with 37 points (8-23 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 17-17 FT), 14 assists and two rebounds across 45 minutes.
news.story: Young struggled from two-point range, but he was productive from downtown and didn't miss a shot at the charity stripe, finishing with a team- and season-high scoring total. The star floor general also dished out a game- and season-best 14 assists, securing his fifth double-double of the campaign. The 28-year-old has reached the 20-point mark in three of his last five outings and has knocked down at least three triples in four of them.

news.headline: Young ended with 20 points (6-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 5-9 FT), one rebound, seven assists and two steals across 38 minutes during Monday's 122-111 loss to Detroit.
news.story: Young was inefficient from the field and the free-throw line, but he reached 20 points and led Washington in assists. Playing alongside Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa has cut into his scoring opportunities, though Young's role as the primary facilitator keeps his fantasy floor steady.

news.headline: Young finished with four points (1-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: Young turned in a lackluster all-around performance, delivering his lowest point total in a game since Nov. 4, 2024, when he recorded just two points in 23 minutes. The star floor general also delivered a season low in assists. In four outings so far this month, Young has averaged 15.0 points, 7.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals across 33.3 minutes per contest.

news.headline: VanVleet (knee) is off the injury report for Monday's game against Miami.
news.story: Coming off 2025 ACL surgery, the veteran point guard sat out the front end of this back-to-back set but is good to go for the second part Monday. Reed Sheppard should fall into a lesser role with VanVleet back in the fold, though Amen Thompson (knee) is questionable.

news.headline: VanVleet (right knee injury management) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
news.story: VanVleet will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set, with his next opportunity to play coming Monday at Miami. With the veteran floor general sidelined, Reed Sheppard, Bogdan Bogdanovic and Bruce Thornton are candidates for increased playing time, while Amen Thompson figures to see increased on-ball duties.

news.headline: VanVleet had 18 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, six assists and three steals over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 victory over Golden State.
news.story: The veteran point guard contributed at both ends of the court, as he drained multiple three-pointers for the seventh straight appearance. VanVleet did get held out for the second game of a back-to-back during that period, something that will likely continue to happen all season. Regardless, over that stretch, he's averaging 16.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.4 threes, 3.1 boards and 1.0 steals while shooting 41.4 percent from long range.

news.headline: Lendeborg amassed 25 points (9-19 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-8 FT), 10 rebounds and two steals over 36 minutes in Wednesday's 115-108 loss to the Rockets.
news.story: This was Lendeborg's third straight 20-plus-point performance and the third double-double of his career. The rookie ranks inside the top-50 of all players on the season with averages of 21.7 points, 7.4 rebounds, 3.7 assists, 2.4 triples, 1.1 steals and 0.7 swats per contest on 51.8 percent shooting from the field and 74.3 percent at the line.

news.headline: Lendeborg totaled 23 points (8-10 FG, 4-4 3Pt, 3-4 FT), seven rebounds, four assists and one steal over 27 minutes during Monday's 138-87 win over New Orleans.
news.story: Lendeborg was nearly flawless from the field, hitting all four of his three-point attempts. He also filled the box score in just 27 minutes. The rookie continues to look like the Warriors' No. 2 option behind Stephen Curry, and his all-around production should keep him in standard lineups. The lopsided score kept Lendeborg's minutes in check, but he still did plenty even in limited action.

news.headline: Green recorded two points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), six rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and two blocks across 34 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
news.story: Green overcame a nearly nonexistent scoring contribution by delivering outstanding playmaking and defensive production. His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is available for Saturday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Green will power through the elbow issue and make himself available for Saturday's game. The 36-year-old forward is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.8 stocks per contest this season.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.
news.story: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

news.headline: Clingan contributed 13 points (6-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt), 11 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two steals across 27 minutes during Friday's 120-107 win over the Kings.
news.story: Clingan posted a double-double while adding two blocks. The young center wasn't as efficient as usual, but his size made a difference in the paint, especially against Domantas Sabonis. Clingan will have a tough matchup in Minnesota early next week.

news.headline: Clingan totaled seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), 13 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 26 minutes during Tuesday's 123-103 win over Oklahoma City.
news.story: Clingan didn't score much, but he controlled the glass and protected the rim against an undersized Thunder frontcourt. That's exactly the role Portland needs from him, and he'll be a matchup problem for Oklahoma City again Wednesday.

news.story: Flagg struggled to establish himself offensively, attempting only 12 shots as Dallas fell behind early and didn't recover. His seven rebounds and two steals helped preserve some fantasy value despite the modest scoring output, but fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about one bad game. Flagg has had some inconsistencies, but for the most part, his numbers have been excellent. He has surpassed the 20-point mark in seven of his 11 appearances, averaging 6.9 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 2.2 steals per contest.

news.headline: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: Irving was listed as questionable to face Boston after playing 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss in Cleveland. He will, however, sit out the second leg of the back-to-back for Dallas, which will likely send Cooper Flagg's usage to the moon. Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton should also get a boost in minutes and playmaking responsibilities off the bench.

news.headline: Irving (knee) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Celtics.
news.story: Irving poured in a game-high 34 points in 37 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 loss to Cleveland, so there's a decent chance Dallas will give its star point guard the night off for the second leg of their back-to-back set. If he is indeed out, Cooper Flagg's usage would see a massive boost while Naji Marshall and Walter Clayton Jr. would figure to earn more minutes off the bench.

news.headline: Irving ended with 34 points (11-25 FG, 7-16 3Pt, 5-7 FT), six rebounds, five assists, three steals and one block over 37 minutes in Saturday's 127-117 loss to Cleveland.
news.story: Irving finished with at least 30 points for the second time in his last three games. He also remained active defensively, recording a block for the second consecutive contest while garnering three steals for the second time in November. The 34-year-old veteran had a slow start to the 2026-27 campaign after missing last season while recovering from knee surgery. In 11 regular-season appearances, Irving is now averaging 22.7 points, 3.5 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals while shooting 39.8 percent from deep across 30.7 minutes per outing.

news.headline: Grimes (finger) is available to play in Sunday's game against the Suns.
news.story: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games due to a right finger splint, but he's going to give it a go versus Phoenix. With Austin Reaves (heel) ruled out and Collin Sexton (eye) questionable, Grimes could step into the starting lineup. We'll have to wait for confirmation from LA prior to tipoff, but either way, he should see a bump in minutes.

news.headline: Grimes (finger) said he expects to return to action Sunday against the Suns, according to Ricardo Sandoval of Lakers on SI.
news.story: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games, but it sounds as if he could return to the rotation Sunday. It's unclear whether he'd be a starter, but he'd have a chance if Austin Reaves (heel) isn't cleared. Grimes is averaging 8.0 points per game this season, but that number rises to 17.5 points per game in his two starts.

Mara has taken on a more consistent role while Jaylin Williams (back) has been sidelined, starting four of the last seven games and averaging 25.0 minutes, 11.9 points, 7.4 boards, 1.7 assists and 1.7 blocks over that stretch while shooting 67.9 percent from the floor.

news.story: Mara will shift to a reserve role Sunday, with Ajay Mitchell (ankle) returning to the lineup. Mara has scored in double figures in each of his last four appearances, averaging 12.3 points, 6.8 rebounds, 2.0 blocks and 1.8 assists in 26.5 minutes per contest.

news.story: That's now back-to-back double-doubles for Zubac, who appears to be just about all the way back from a recent extended absence due to an ankle sprain. The veteran big man has played at least 26 minutes in three consecutive appearances, posting a double-double in three of his last four outings.

news.story: Hield rejoined the rotation, scoring in double figures for just the second time this season. The veteran wing has a chance to carve out a more meaningful role moving forward, as Caleb Wilson (hand) is set to miss an extended period.

news.story: After scoring 13 points on 5-of-6 shooting in Friday's win over Milwaukee, Hield once again provided a spark off the bench Saturday. The veteran shooting guard is averaging 7.3 points and 2.0 rebounds in 15.0 minutes per contest across three regular-season games.

news.story: The veteran wing was picked up from the Hornets at the end of September to provide some experience and a moveable contract to the Bulls' second unit, but while he's with Chicago, Hield's long-range shooting will help spread the floor for young building blocks like Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson. news.headline: Acuff finished Friday's 120-107 loss to the Trail Blazers with 17 points (6-19 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 2-2 FT), four rebounds, six assists and two steals over 35 minutes.
news.story: The rookie had to work for his 17 points Friday, needing 19 shots and going just 3-for-10 from deep, though he matched Zach LaVine for the team lead with six assists. Acuff has been handed a lot of responsibility on a struggling Kings team, and nights like this are part of the learning curve. Sacramento has now lost five straight and is still winless at home, so his minutes aren't going anywhere. Next up is a tough Sunday matchup with Oklahoma City.

news.headline: Clingan contributed 13 points (6-13 FG, 1-4 3Pt), 11 rebounds, two assists, two blocks and two steals across 27 minutes during Friday's 120-107 win over the Kings.
news.story: Clingan posted a double-double while adding two blocks. The young center wasn't as efficient as usual, but his size made a difference in the paint, especially against Domantas Sabonis. Clingan will have a tough matchup in Minnesota early next week.

news.headline: Clingan totaled seven points (3-6 FG, 1-2 3Pt), 13 rebounds, three assists and two blocks over 26 minutes during Tuesday's 123-103 win over Oklahoma City.
news.story: Clingan didn't score much, but he controlled the glass and protected the rim against an undersized Thunder frontcourt. That's exactly the role Portland needs from him, and he'll be a matchup problem for Oklahoma City again Wednesday.

news.headline: Green recorded two points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), six rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and two blocks across 34 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
news.story: Green overcame a nearly nonexistent scoring contribution by delivering outstanding playmaking and defensive production. His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is available for Saturday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Green will power through the elbow issue and make himself available for Saturday's game. The 36-year-old forward is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.8 stocks per contest this season.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.
news.story: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

news.story: Coming off 2025 ACL surgery, the veteran point guard sat out the front end of this back-to-back set but is good to go for the second part Monday. Reed Sheppard should fall into a lesser role with VanVleet back in the fold, though Amen Thompson (knee) is questionable.

news.headline: VanVleet (right knee injury management) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
news.story: VanVleet will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set, with his next opportunity to play coming Monday at Miami. With the veteran floor general sidelined, Reed Sheppard, Bogdan Bogdanovic and Bruce Thornton are candidates for increased playing time, while Amen Thompson figures to see increased on-ball duties.

news.headline: VanVleet had 18 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, six assists and three steals over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 victory over Golden State.
news.story: The veteran point guard contributed at both ends of the court, as he drained multiple three-pointers for the seventh straight appearance. VanVleet did get held out for the second game of a back-to-back during that period, something that will likely continue to happen all season. Regardless, over that stretch, he's averaging 16.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.4 threes, 3.1 boards and 1.0 steals while shooting 41.4 percent from long range.

news.headline: Zubac supplied 12 points (6-12 FG), 13 rebounds, one assist and one block in 26 minutes during Friday's 106-104 win over the Knicks.
news.story: That's now back-to-back double-doubles for Zubac, who appears to be just about all the way back from a recent extended absence due to an ankle sprain. The veteran big man has played at least 26 minutes in three consecutive appearances, posting a double-double in three of his last four outings.

news.story: Zubac scored efficiently around the basket, converting five of seven field-goal attempts and making six free throws. However, his three rebounds were disappointing for a starting center, and he recorded no defensive stats. Zubac's fantasy value remains closely tied to rebounding and field-goal efficiency, making this a relatively underwhelming performance despite his scoring contribution.

news.headline: Grimes (finger) is available to play in Sunday's game against the Suns.
news.story: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games due to a right finger splint, but he's going to give it a go versus Phoenix. With Austin Reaves (heel) ruled out and Collin Sexton (eye) questionable, Grimes could step into the starting lineup. We'll have to wait for confirmation from LA prior to tipoff, but either way, he should see a bump in minutes.

news.story: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games, but it sounds as if he could return to the rotation Sunday. news.story: Gobert controlled the glass, grabbing a game-high 15 rebounds while converting all four of his field-goal attempts. The veteran center recorded his double-double despite failing to register a steal or block, limiting his overall fantasy production. Gobert remains a dependable source of rebounds and field-goal percentage, with his defensive contributions typically providing additional upside.

news.headline: Young finished Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons with 37 points (8-23 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 17-17 FT), 14 assists and two rebounds across 45 minutes.
news.story: Young struggled from two-point range, but he was productive from downtown and didn't miss a shot at the charity stripe, finishing with a team- and season-high scoring total. news.story: Young was inefficient from the field and the free-throw line, but he reached 20 points and led Washington in assists. Playing alongside Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa has cut into his scoring opportunities, though Young's role as the primary facilitator keeps his fantasy floor steady.

news.headline: Young finished with four points (1-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: Young turned in a lackluster all-around performance, delivering his lowest point total in a game since Nov. 4, 2024, when he recorded just two points in 23 minutes. news.story: This was Lendeborg's third straight 20-plus-point performance and the third double-double of his career. news.story: Lendeborg was nearly flawless from the field, hitting all four of his three-point attempts. He also filled the box score in just 27 minutes. news.story: This was the expectation after Murray requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Shams Charania of ESPN noted Friday that the star guard won't be available for New Orleans for the time being, so Murray can be considered out indefinitely while the team tries to find him another home.

news.headline: Murray (ankle) requested a trade from the Pelicans on Friday, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
news.story: Charania also notes Murray's agent and team officials have begun working toward a resolution. Murray, who's listed as doubtful for Friday's game against Memphis with an ankle sprain, could miss more time beyond that while New Orleans looks to find him a new destination. Murray, a one-time All-Star, has been limited to 54 regular-season appearances in his Pelicans career, but he's averaged a strong 16.6 points, 6.6 assists, 5.9 rebounds and 1.9 steals per game across that three-year span.

news.story: Murray is likely to sit out the front end of this back-to-back set with an ankle sprain. Saddiq Bey stands out as the most likely choice to join the starting lineup in Murray's stead.

news.headline: Portis produced five points (2-6 FG, 1-3 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists across 15 minutes during Friday's 133-121 win over the Cavaliers.
news.story: Portis' shooting woes continued Friday, and he's now shot just 27.6 percent from the field through six games this month. The veteran big man has averaged 3.3 points and 3.8 rebounds across 17.0 minutes per tilt over that stretch.

news.headline: Portis ended with two points (1-3 FG, 0-2 3Pt), three rebounds and two assists in 18 minutes during Monday's 138-117 loss to the Lakers.
news.story: After scoring at least seven points in each of his first six appearances, Portis cooled down a bit Monday. The veteran big man has one double-double on the year but has yet to score at least 15 points, and his production could remain erratic while Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo are healthy.

news.headline: Portis notched 11 points (5-11 FG, 1-5 3Pt), nine rebounds, four assists, one block and two steals across 23 minutes during Wednesday's 129-117 victory over the Hawks.
news.story: Portis made his presence felt across several categories despite struggling from beyond the arc. The veteran forward finished one rebound shy of a double-double while contributing three defensive statistics, making this a productive outing in limited minutes. His ability to provide rebounding and complementary scoring off the bench should help maintain his fantasy appeal, though Miami's crowded frontcourt could limit his ceiling.

news.headline: Hield amassed 12 points (5-10 FG, 2-7 3Pt), three rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block over 25 minutes during Friday's 125-117 overtime win over the Hawks.
news.story: Hield rejoined the rotation, scoring in double figures for just the second time this season. The veteran wing has a chance to carve out a more meaningful role moving forward, as Caleb Wilson (hand) is set to miss an extended period.

news.headline: Hield had nine points (4-7 FG, 1-3 3Pt), two rebounds and two assists in 16 minutes during Saturday's 124-120 loss to the Wizards.
news.story: After scoring 13 points on 5-of-6 shooting in Friday's win over Milwaukee, Hield once again provided a spark off the bench Saturday. The veteran shooting guard is averaging 7.3 points and 2.0 rebounds in 15.0 minutes per contest across three regular-season games.

news.headline: Hield produced 15 points (4-7 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 3-3 FT), three rebounds, two steals and an assist in 19 minutes off the bench during Sunday's 133-128 preseason loss to the Nuggets.
news.story: The veteran wing was picked up from the Hornets at the end of September to provide some experience and a moveable contract to the Bulls' second unit, but while he's with Chicago, Hield's long-range shooting will help spread the floor for young building blocks like Matas Buzelis and Caleb Wilson. Hield's coming off a disappointing 2025-26 campaign split between Atlanta and Golden State, but prior to last season he hadn't shot below 36.6 percent from three-point range or averaged fewer than 2.2 threes in any of the prior eight seasons.

news.headline: Murray-Boyles ended with 14 points (5-9 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four assists, five blocks and one steal over 32 minutes during Thursday's 123-112 loss to the 76ers.
news.story: Murray-Boyles made up for a rough showing in Wednesday's 98-93 loss to the Celtics with a career-high-tying five blocks. However, he did fail to record a rebound despite playing 30-plus minutes, making it the second-year Raptors' first such outing this season. Murray-Boyles could continue providing solid fantasy contributions across several categories, especially if his minutes keep climbing with Scottie Barnes (groin) and Kawhi Leonard (knee) sidelined.

news.headline: Smith tallied 14 points (6-13 FG, 2-8 3Pt), seven rebounds and three assists across 38 minutes in Monday's 110-100 win over the Nuggets.
news.story: Smith maintained a heavy workload, and while his perimeter shooting was subpar, he still posted a solid line across the board, finishing just three boards shy of a double-double. Smith's value in category formats depends on improved three-point efficiency and more consistent contributions in steals and blocks, but he has a solid foundation. He has recorded at least 14 points and seven rebounds in four of his last five appearances.

news.headline: Smith racked up 15 points (7-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt), nine rebounds, two assists, one block and three steals over 39 minutes during Saturday's 102-99 loss to Phoenix.
news.story: After failing to record any steals in his previous three outings, Smith ripped away a season-high three swipes Saturday, and this was his fourth game of the season with at least one steal and block. He's producing a career-worst 11.8 points per game, and he's been limited to 12 points or fewer in each of his last three games and in four of his last five outings. There's still upside if his offensive responsibilities grow, but he's currently more of a speculative hold than a dependable fantasy starter, given his prolonged struggles.

news.story: Green shot efficiently from the field, but his playing time was capped at 21 minutes with Phoenix comfortably ahead for much of the second half. After missing nearly the entire 2025-26 campaign, Green has the scoring upside to make an impact in fantasy, but his lack of peripheral production limits his overall value. Assuming he returns to his usual workload in more competitive matchups, he should remain rostered in most formats as a points-and-threes asset.

news.story: Harden will miss his first game of the season due to a calf issue he picked up sometime after Friday's loss to Miami. Fellow guard Donovan Mitchell (knee) will also be inactive Saturday, leaving Tyrese Proctor, Craig Porter and Meleek Thomas as Cleveland's top backcourt options.

news.story: Allen will get a break to rest his injured right knee after playing in each of Cleveland's last three games. With Evan Mobley (toe) also out, Thomas Bryant can be expected to take on a larger role Saturday.

news.headline: Allen (knee) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Dallas.
news.story: Allen has played in each of Cleveland's last three games after sitting out two contests with a right knee injury, but lingering issues have now put his availability for Saturday's game in jeopardy. Thomas Bryant and Mario Hezonja could take on increased playing time if Allen ends up sitting.

news.headline: Kuminga closed Friday's 115-109 win over the Pelicans with 17 points (5-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 6-12 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one steal in 34 minutes.
news.story: The 24-year-old forward has been one of the bigger beneficiaries of the shot volume that opened up when Anthony Edwards (knee) was shut down. Kuminga is averaging nearly three shots a game more without Edwards on the court, averaging 14.2 points, 6.0 boards, 3.3 assists, 2.2 threes and 1.9 combined blocks and steals in six games since the Minnesota superstar went for surgery. There could be more meat on the bone for Kuminga as well, as his 42.9 percent FG shooting over that stretch would be a career-low mark.

Durant has scored 20-plus points in each of his last five outings, and he has averaged 21.4 points, 6.8 rebounds and 4.8 assists over 35.1 minutes per game during that stretch, although he's connected on only 41.9 percent of his field-goal attempts in that span (including 30.4 percent from three on 4.6 3PA/G).

news.story: Kuzma delivered an impressive scoring performance, connecting on six three-pointers while adding three combined steals-plus-blocks. This 27-point output was not only Kuzma's best scoring output of the season, but it also represented the first time he's scored at least 20 points in the current campaign. Kuzma is averaging just 12.4 points per game over his last five appearances, so this was likely a one-game outlier rather than a sign of what's to come.

news.headline: Kuzma ended with two points (1-6 FG, 0-4 3Pt), two rebounds, three assists and one steal over 22 minutes during Monday's 112-100 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Kuzma endured another frustrating offensive outing, missing all four of his three-point attempts while finishing with a team-worst minus-22 rating. He attempted just six shots despite starting, while Milwaukee received more productive performances from Jaime Jaquez and its reserves. Kuzma's limited playing time and inconsistent scoring make him difficult to trust in standard fantasy formats.

news.story: Kuzma delivered his strongest contribution on the glass, collecting 12 rebounds while playing a team-high 35 minutes. However, his scoring remained modest, and he failed to register a steal or block. His substantial workload offers some fantasy stability, but with Milwaukee featuring several offensive options, Kuzma may need consistent rebounding to compensate for the ups and downs in his scoring production. He's yet to reach the 15-point mark despite playing at least 27 minutes in every game.

news.headline: Washington accumulated 10 points (4-7 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 1-1 FT) and three rebounds over 16 minutes during Thursday's 133-94 loss to Minnesota.
news.story: Washington's workload was his biggest obstacle, as he played just over 16 minutes and failed to register an assist or defensive stat in a 39-point Mavs loss. His efficient overall shooting provided little consolation for fantasy managers. The blowout contributed to his reduced opportunities, but his rebounding and defensive production will need to improve for him to maintain consistent category-league value, especially when considering he's now logged 25 minutes or fewer in two of his last three appearances.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander logged 37 points (13-20 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 7-7 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 29 minutes during Sunday's 125-103 win over the Kings.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander came in with a pure scorer's mindset Sunday, getting off to a fast start with 20 first-half points without recording an assist. It was a lot of the same in the second half, as the star guard finished with a game-high 37 points. While he only contributed two assists, Gilgeous-Alexander impressively did not commit a turnover during Sunday's contest. He has now scored at least 30 points in four of his last five games.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday's 113-112 loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-26 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 8-11 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal in 38 minutes.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander did everything he could to carry a shorthanded Oklahoma City team, scoring 40 points and hitting a leaning three that put the Thunder up four with three minutes left. He had a chance to win it at the buzzer, but his 21-foot jumper missed, and the Thunder dropped a season-high third straight game. With Chet Holmgren (knee), Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) all out since late October, nearly every possession runs through Gilgeous-Alexander. That workload won't ease up Sunday at Sacramento.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander posted 31 points (9-20 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 13-14 FT), four rebounds, two assists and a steal across 36 minutes in Wednesday's 118-108 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander overcame a difficult perimeter shooting performance by getting to the free-throw line consistently, converting 13 of 14 attempts en route to posting a seventh consecutive game with at least 25 points. However, his two assists were unusually modest, limiting his overall fantasy production despite the strong scoring output. Fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much, as Gilgeous-Alexander remains one of the best and most reliable fantasy options.

news.headline: George provided 13 points (5-17 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), eight assists and four rebounds over 34 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 loss to San Antonio.
news.story: George struggled with efficiency, especially from beyond the arc. However, he still finished as one of four Jazz players to score in double figures while pacing the team in assists. The 23-year-old has dished out at least seven dimes in six straight games, averaging 21.2 points, 8.0 assists, 4.7 rebounds and 1.2 steals across 35.2 minutes per game over that period.

news.headline: George finished Friday's 125-118 loss to the Rockets with 27 points (8-17 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 7-8 FT), seven assists, six rebounds and one steal over 37 minutes.
news.story: George had a quiet first half with only four points while missing four of his five field-goal attempts. However, the fourth-year pro found his form in the second half, when he scored 10 and 13 points in the third and fourth quarters, respectively, to help the Jazz stay in the game. Utah's future was shining bright during Friday's loss, with George, 2025 fifth-overall pick Ace Bailey and rookie second overall selection Darryn Peterson each scoring 20-plus points. For the season, George is averaging 20.9 points, 6.5 assists, 4.6 rebounds, 2.0 threes and 0.9 steals over 32.6 minutes per game.

news.headline: George (ankle) is available for Wednesday's game against the Magic.
news.story: George is back after a one-game absence. His return will likely push Josh Okogie back to the second unit, and Isaiah Collier's minutes will likely dip. With Lauri Markkanen (hand) set to miss at least the next month, George should be operating with a hefty usage rate moving forward.

news.headline: Proctor posted 24 points (10-19 FG, 4-13 3Pt), 11 rebounds and 10 assists across 34 minutes during Saturday's 127-117 win over Dallas.
news.story: Proctor earned his second start of the season and more than delivered for a short-handed Cavs team, as the 2025 second-round pick recorded the first triple-double of his career. The performance is even more impressive when considering Cleveland was without all of James Harden (calf), Donovan Mitchell (knee), Jarrett Allen (knee), Evan Mobley (toe), Sam Merrill (elbow) and Peyton Watson (hamstring). Prior to Saturday's victory, Proctor averaged 8.1 points, 2.9 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.6 three-pointers in 17.9 minutes over 12 outings. He's proven himself as an important role player for a Cava

news.headline: Proctor will start in Saturday's game versus the Mavericks.
news.story: The Cavaliers' starters won't suit up for this contest, so Proctor will enter the starting lineup Saturday for the second time this season. The 22-year-old started in the 124-116 loss to the Thunder on Nov. 4, and he finished that game with 11 points and one rebound over 22 minutes of work.

news.headline: Proctor recorded 22 points (7-9 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 27 minutes during Friday's 133-121 loss to the Heat.
news.story: Proctor made the most of his minutes and matched his previous career-high mark in scoring, but five three-pointers on seven attempts isn't a realistic nightly expectation. The more encouraging development is that Cleveland trusted him with a heavy workload, even with Donovan Mitchell and James Harden available. Proctor's role remains relatively modest behind Cleveland's established guards, making consistent fantasy production difficult to project. However, performances like Friday's could strengthen his case for additional minutes as the season progresses.

news.headline: McDaniels delivered 18 points (7-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, six assists, two steals and a block across 37 minutes in Saturday's 117-106 loss to the Bulls.
news.story: McDaniels was one of Minnesota's few efficient offensive performers, and his six assists were particularly encouraging for a forward who typically contributes more through scoring and defense. He has now scored 16 and 18 points in his last two outings, respectively, while continuing to see substantial minutes. With Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined, McDaniels has additional opportunities to contribute offensively, although his defensive versatility remains the foundation of his fantasy value.

news.headline: McDaniels finished with 16 points (5-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 33 minutes in Sunday's 115-100 win over the Jazz.
news.story: McDaniels delivered an efficient all-around performance, contributing in every major statistical category while maintaining a substantial workload. His two made three-pointers and perfect free-throw shooting strengthened his offensive efficiency, while his defensive contributions provided additional value. McDaniels remains particularly useful in category formats, where his versatility can compensate for inconsistent scoring volume.

news.headline: McDaniels finished with 23 points (8-19 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and two blocks over 40 minutes in Friday's 115-109 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: McDaniels snapped a three-game swat-less streak during Friday's win, and he got some triples to drop after going 0-for-7 from beyond the arc in his previous outing. The 26-year-old vet is off to his best start yet, averaging 17.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.4 triples, and 1.7 stocks per contest, which has him flirting with top-50 value on the year.

news.headline: Watson (abdomen) will play in Monday's game against the Bulls, Danny Cunningham of Sports Radio 92.3 The Fan Cleveland reports.
news.story: The defensive-minded forward is returning Monday from a one-game respite due to abdominal soreness. Watson's return likely takes away a starting spot from either Mario Hezonja or Meleek Thomas.

news.headline: Watson (abdominal soreness) is questionable to play in Monday's game against the Bulls.
news.story: Watson missed Saturday's 127-117 win over Dallas due to a hamstring injury, but he's now dealing with right abdominal soreness. Tyrese Proctor, Mario Hezonja and Meleek Thomas will see an uptick in minutes if Watson remains sidelined Monday.

news.headline: Watson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Mavericks.
news.story: Watson will join the rest of Cleveland's regular starters on the inactive list. The 24-year-old's next chance to play will come Monday against Chicago. With Watson sidelined, Jaylon Tyson and Mario Hezonja will likely see increased playing time.

news.headline: Sengun closed with 19 points (5-8 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 8-9 FT), eight rebounds, eight assists and two steals in 28 minutes during Sunday's 147-119 win over the Wizards.
news.story: Sengun came within two rebounds and two assists of a triple-double despite playing fewer than 30 minutes, a perfect example of his efficiency in a huge win for Houston. His eight assists were particularly impressive in a game where the Rockets distributed the ball exceptionally well, finishing with 40 assists as a team. Sengun's development as a facilitator continues to distinguish him from traditional centers, and his ability to contribute in scoring, rebounding and playmaking gives him a strong fantasy foundation even when his shot volume is relatively modest. He's averaging a robust 22.2 po

news.headline: Sengun finished with 43 points (17-24 FG, 1-3 3Pt, 8-12 FT), 12 rebounds, five assists, one steal and one block across 37 minutes in Friday's 125-118 win over the Jazz.
news.story: Sengun was virtually unstoppable offensively, shooting 70.8 percent from the field while leading all scorers with 43 points. The versatile big man also paced Houston with 12 rebounds and contributed five assists, delivering an outstanding all-around fantasy performance. Sengun's offensive dominance was particularly important on a night when Kevin Durant shot just 5-for-14 from the field, and the former's ability to produce elite numbers across multiple categories continues to make him a cornerstone fantasy option.

news.headline: Edgecombe had 11 points (5-11 FG, 0-4 3Pt, 1-2 FT), six assists, four rebounds and one steal in 31 minutes during Sunday's 131-124 victory over the Pacers.
news.story: Edgecombe struggled from three-point range but turned in a productive all-around outing, tying for second on the team in assists while scoring in double figures. The second-year swingman has dished out at least five dimes in three straight games. Through seven appearances in November, he's averaged 14.0 points, 4.9 rebounds, 4.6 assists and 2.0 steals across 33.4 minutes per tilt.

news.headline: Edgecombe finished with 15 points (7-12 FG, 1-4 3Pt), eight rebounds, eight assists, one block and three steals in 36 minutes during Thursday's 123-112 victory over the Raptors.
news.story: Edgecombe struggled in Tuesday's 123-101 loss to the Celtics, finishing with an 8/4/5/1/1 line on 4-for-11 shooting and 0-for-4 from behind the arc, but he was sensational Thursday. He tied for the team lead in rebounds and assists while committing zero turnovers, and he racked up four stocks by tallying his third outing with at least three swipes in the last four games. Edgecombe should continue to be a valuable fantasy asset due to his ability to contribute in every category.

news.headline: Green recorded two points (1-5 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 0-2 FT), six rebounds, 13 assists, two steals and two blocks across 34 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime win over the Magic.
news.story: Green overcame a nearly nonexistent scoring contribution by delivering outstanding playmaking and defensive production. His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is available for Saturday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Green will power through the elbow issue and make himself available for Saturday's game. The 36-year-old forward is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.8 stocks per contest this season.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.
news.story: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

news.headline: Flagg contributed 17 points (5-15 FG, 2-6 3Pt, 5-5 FT), three rebounds, four assists, one block and one steal in 27 minutes during Sunday's 131-94 loss to the Celtics.
news.story: Dallas fell behind 42-9 in the first quarter and never recovered, and the nature of the game conspired against Flagg's chances to make a big impact. The reigning Rookie of the Year has now endured three consecutive losses on the Mavericks' road trip, with Dallas losing those contests by a combined 86 points. His offensive responsibilities remain substantial in his second NBA season, but Sunday's inefficient performance illustrates how difficult it can be to maintain consistent production when the entire team struggles to generate quality looks. news.headline: Flagg chipped in 12 points (5-12 FG, 1-2 3Pt, 1-2 FT), seven rebounds, three assists and two steals over 27 minutes during Thursday's 133-94 loss to the Timberwolves.
news.story: Flagg struggled to establish himself offensively, attempting only 12 shots as Dallas fell behind early and didn't recover. His seven rebounds and two steals helped preserve some fantasy value despite the modest scoring output, but fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much about one bad game. Flagg has had some inconsistencies, but for the most part, his numbers have been excellent. He has surpassed the 20-point mark in seven of his 11 appearances, averaging 6.9 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 2.2 steals per contest.

news.headline: Brown tallied 31 points (12-18 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Sunday's 131-124 win over Indiana.
news.story: Brown cooked for an efficient 31 points on 18 shot attempts to set a new season high in scoring, and he also recorded at least one steal for the eighth straight contest. The first-year Sixer has led his team in scoring four out of the last six games after combining for 31 total points over his previous two outings. Brown is shooting 52.5 percent from the field in seven November appearances, and he's averaging 22.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.3 steals and 2.0 three-pointers in 33.3 minutes this month.

news.headline: Brown ended Tuesday's 123-101 loss to the Celtics with 13 points (4-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals in 26 minutes.
news.story: Brown endured a disappointing first matchup against Boston since his offseason trade, attempting just nine shots while committing four turnovers. His three combined defensive stats helped salvage some fantasy value, but foul trouble and the lopsided result restricted his workload. Brown's scoring upside remains substantial, but this was a down performance, as it ended a streak of four games in a row in which he had reached the 20-point plateau.

news.headline: Castle had 20 points (6-11 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 8-9 FT), nine assists, four rebounds and four steals across 35 minutes during Sunday's 110-102 victory over the Jazz.
news.story: With De'Aaron Fox (hip) sidelined, Castle took on increased playmaking duties, dishing out a game- and season-high nine assists. The third-year guard also reached the 20-point threshold for a second straight game while tallying a game-high mark in steals. In eight outings this month, he's averaged 16.6 points, 5.5 assists, 5.3 rebounds and 0.9 steals across 29.0 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Castle finished Friday's 123-85 victory over the Warriors with 32 points (12-18 FG, 5-8 3Pt, 3-3 FT), five rebounds, six assists and one block in 25 minutes.
news.story: Castle was the story of the night, scoring a season-high 32 points. His previous best this season was 24 on Opening Night against Oklahoma City, and he blew past it before the fourth quarter started. If his shots keep falling like this, the third-year guard could become a real problem for defenses already worried about Victor Wembanyama.

news.headline: Grimes will start in Sunday's game versus the Suns, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
news.story: With Austin Reaves (heel) sidelined, Grimes will start Sunday. In two starts during the 2026-27 campaign, the 26-year-old is averaging 17.5 points, 2.0 rebounds, 4.5 assists and 2.5 steals over 35.0 minutes per contest.

news.headline: Grimes (finger) is available to play in Sunday's game against the Suns.
news.story: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games due to a right finger splint, but he's going to give it a go versus Phoenix. With Austin Reaves (heel) ruled out and Collin Sexton (eye) questionable, Grimes could step into the starting lineup. We'll have to wait for confirmation from LA prior to tipoff, but either way, he should see a bump in minutes.

news.headline: Grimes (finger) said he expects to return to action Sunday against the Suns, according to Ricardo Sandoval of Lakers on SI.
news.story: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games, but it sounds as if he could return to the rotation Sunday. It's unclear whether he'd be a starter, but he'd have a chance if Austin Reaves (heel) isn't cleared. Grimes is averaging 8.0 points per game this season, but that number rises to 17.5 points per game in his two starts.

news.headline: Williams will start Monday's game against the Hawks.
news.story: With Austin Reaves (illness) and Quentin Grimes (finger) sidelined, Williams will join the first unit for the first time since Oct. 27. In four starts this season, he's averaged 11.3 points, 3.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals across 28.5 minutes per tilt.

news.headline: Williams accumulated eight points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 20 minutes during Friday's 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Williams gave the Lakers useful minutes off the bench, knocking down a pair of three-pointers and picking up two steals in his 20 minutes. The forward missed three straight games with soreness in his left foot, an issue going back to the preseason, before being cleared to return earlier in the week. The Lakers begin a back-to-back Sunday, so he could be held out for one of those games.

news.headline: Ware won't start Friday's game against the Magic.
news.story: With Myles Turner (rest) back in action, Ware will slide to the second unit. The 22-year-old center has averaged 3.2 points, 4.2 rebounds and 1.2 blocks across 14.4 minutes per game in his last five outings off the bench.

news.headline: Young finished Thursday's 144-140 double-overtime loss to the Pistons with 37 points (8-23 FG, 4-8 3Pt, 17-17 FT), 14 assists and two rebounds across 45 minutes.
news.story: Young struggled from two-point range, but he was productive from downtown and didn't miss a shot at the charity stripe, finishing with a team- and season-high scoring total. The star floor general also dished out a game- and season-best 14 assists, securing his fifth double-double of the campaign. The 28-year-old has reached the 20-point mark in three of his last five outings and has knocked down at least three triples in four of them.

news.headline: Young ended with 20 points (6-17 FG, 3-10 3Pt, 5-9 FT), one rebound, seven assists and two steals across 38 minutes during Monday's 122-111 loss to Detroit.
news.story: Young was inefficient from the field and the free-throw line, but he reached 20 points and led Washington in assists. Playing alongside Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa has cut into his scoring opportunities, though Young's role as the primary facilitator keeps his fantasy floor steady.

news.headline: Young finished with four points (1-6 FG, 0-1 3Pt, 2-3 FT), five rebounds, three assists and one steal in 28 minutes during Saturday's 114-75 loss to the Thunder.
news.story: Young turned in a lackluster all-around performance, delivering his lowest point total in a game since Nov. 4, 2024, when he recorded just two points in 23 minutes. The star floor general also delivered a season low in assists. In four outings so far this month, Young has averaged 15.0 points, 7.0 assists, 3.0 rebounds and 1.3 steals across 33.3 minutes per contest.

news.headline: VanVleet (knee) is off the injury report for Monday's game against Miami.
news.story: Coming off 2025 ACL surgery, the veteran point guard sat out the front end of this back-to-back set but is good to go for the second part Monday. Reed Sheppard should fall into a lesser role with VanVleet back in the fold, though Amen Thompson (knee) is questionable.

news.headline: VanVleet (right knee injury management) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Wizards.
news.story: VanVleet will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set, with his next opportunity to play coming Monday at Miami. With the veteran floor general sidelined, Reed Sheppard, Bogdan Bogdanovic and Bruce Thornton are candidates for increased playing time, while Amen Thompson figures to see increased on-ball duties.

news.headline: VanVleet had 18 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, six assists and three steals over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 victory over Golden State.
news.story: The veteran point guard contributed at both ends of the court, as he drained multiple three-pointers for the seventh straight appearance. VanVleet did get held out for the second game of a back-to-back during that period, something that will likely continue to happen all season. Regardless, over that stretch, he's averaging 16.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.4 threes, 3.1 boards and 1.0 steals while shooting 41.4 percent from long range.

news.headline: Brooks totaled 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 30 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 win over the Hornets.
news.story: Brooks has settled into a familiar role in Phoenix, averaging 14.9 points and 3.8 rebounds as a secondary scoring option behind Devin Booker. Brooks' steady minutes and willingness to shoot make him a solid source of points and triples, and he's taken a step forward as a playmaker. His 2.1 assists per game aren't a game-changer, but they're his highest mark in that category since the 2022-23 campaign. As if that wasn't enough, his 3.8 boards per game are a new career-high mark, so Brooks is putting up solid numbers across the board, even if he has a down game from time to time.

news.headline: Brooks notched 11 points (4-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 37 minutes in Saturday's 102-99 win over the Rockets.
news.story: Brooks provided perimeter scoring but little else in this game, failing to record a block or steal and falling short of the 15-point plateau for the first time since the season opener. This was a down game for Brooks, but he remains one of the team's go-to scoring options behind Devin Booker and Jalen Green. At least Brooks has been consistent as a long-range threat and has drained two or more threes in five of his last six outings.

news.headline: Brooks provided 24 points (9-16 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, one assist, one block and two steals across 29 minutes during Thursday's 117-104 win over the Magic.
news.story: Brooks delivered an efficient scoring performance, finishing second on the Suns behind Devin Booker's 30 points. The veteran forward connected on four of his six attempts from beyond the arc while adding three combined steals and blocks. Although Brooks contributed little on the glass or as a facilitator, his scoring, perimeter shooting and defensive production made for a strong fantasy outing.

news.headline: Wagner finished with 35 points (13-22 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 6-6 FT), nine rebounds, 12 assists, one steal and one block across 36 minutes in Friday's 107-99 win over the Bucks.
news.story: Wagner delivered a sensational all-around performance, leading Orlando in scoring and assists while narrowly missing a triple-double. The versatile forward accounted for 25 of the Magic's 41 made field goals through his scoring and playmaking, highlighting his importance to the offense. Wagner continues to provide elite fantasy production across multiple categories, with Friday's outing showcasing his ability to contribute well beyond scoring.

He's been unconscious over that three-game stretch, averaging 33.7 points, 7.0 rebounds, 6.3 assists, 2.3 triples and 1.7 steals per game on 51.5 percent shooting from the field and 96.0 percent at the stripe.

news.headline: Embiid (foot) is available for Monday's game against Brooklyn.
news.story: Embiid sat out Sunday's contest as part of injury management for his right foot, but the big man will return to action for the second half of Philadelphia's back-to-back set. Over his past five games, the 32-year-old is averaging 17.2 points, 8.4 rebounds and 2.4 assists, though he's shooting just 33.3 percent from the field during that stretch.

news.headline: Embiid (foot) is questionable for Monday's game against the Nets.
news.story: Embiid sat out the first half of Philly's back-to-back set Sunday and is now in danger of missing Monday as well. The superstar big man has yet to miss two straight games this season, but if he joins LeBron James (back) in street clothes, Dean Wade, Jabari Walker and Tacko Fall would be candidates for increased roles.

news.headline: Embiid (right foot injury management) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Pacers.
news.story: Embiid will sit out the front end of this back-to-back set. With Adem Bona (back) and Dominick Barlow (back) sidelined, Dean Wade, Jabari Walker and Tacko Fall could all see increased playing time, while LeBron James could see more time at the five as well.

news.story: Fears delivered efficient scoring and solid playmaking despite New Orleans' lopsided defeat. His five assists were encouraging, but four turnovers and a lack of defensive stats reduced his overall fantasy value. Despite the Pelicans' struggles, Fears has posted solid numbers overall as a scoring threat -- he's posted double-digit points in each of his last 10 games while averaging 16.8 points, 5.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists per contest over that stretch.

news.headline: Fears registered 25 points (10-14 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, five assists and two steals across 29 minutes during Sunday's 139-123 loss to the Clippers.
news.story: The second-year guard set a new season scoring high as he delivered at least 20 points for the fourth time in the last six games. Fears has seemingly found his groove in his sophomore campaign, and over that six-game stretch the seventh overall pick in the 2025 Draft is averaging 20.3 points, 6.5 assists, 5.7 boards, 1.5 steals and 1.3 threes while shooting 52.7 percent from the floor.

news.headline: Kuminga closed Friday's 115-109 win over the Pelicans with 17 points (5-12 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 6-12 FT), eight rebounds, four assists and one steal in 34 minutes.
news.story: The 24-year-old forward has been one of the bigger beneficiaries of the shot volume that opened up when Anthony Edwards (knee) was shut down. Kuminga is averaging nearly three shots a game more without Edwards on the court, averaging 14.2 points, 6.0 boards, 3.3 assists, 2.2 threes and 1.9 combined blocks and steals in six games since the Minnesota superstar went for surgery. There could be more meat on the bone for Kuminga as well, as his 42.9 percent FG shooting over that stretch would be a career-low mark.

news.headline: Carter ended with eight points (4-9 FG, 0-2 3Pt), 11 rebounds, one assist, three blocks and one steal in 33 minutes during Tuesday's 107-100 win over the Kings.
news.story: Carter didn't do much on offense, but he did the dirty work in the middle, controlling the boards and protecting the rim. He's been a steady frontcourt presence with Paolo Banchero (ankle) sidelined, and Carter's interior play helps the Magic win even when it doesn't show in the scoring column.

news.headline: Carter registered 19 points (6-12 FG, 3-3 3Pt, 4-9 FT), 11 rebounds and two blocks across 40 minutes in Saturday's 126-119 overtime loss to the Warriors.
news.story: Carter delivered a strong fantasy performance, posting his second consecutive double-double while also tying season-high marks in both made three-pointers and blocks. Carter has found a way to get it done on both ends of the floor this season, and he's recorded either double-digit points or double-digit rebounds in all but one of his nine outings in 2026-27. He's averaging 14.8 points and 9.6 boards per contest and is emerging as a reliable middle-tier option at center.

news.story: Gordon was questionable to play versus the Rockets due to left calf injury management, but he's good to suit up and reprise his role in Denver's starting unit.

news.headline: Gordon (left calf injury management) has been upgraded to probable for Monday's game against Houston.
news.story: Gordon appears likely to play despite ongoing management of his left calf injury. His expected presence should bolster Denver's frontcourt rotation, particularly with Julian Strawther (knee) sidelined. Gordon's combination of scoring, rebounding and defensive contributions makes him a useful fantasy option when healthy, though his workload will be worth monitoring.

news.headline: Gordon (lower body injury management) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets.
news.story: Along with Nikola Jokic (elbow), Jamal Murray (shin), Christian Braun (calf/illness), Cameron Johnson (lower body) and DeMar DeRozan (back), Gordon is questionable to play Monday. If the veteran forward is unable to go, Trevon Brazile, Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo would be candidates for increased playing time.

news.headline: Demin (leg) closed Wednesday's 145-111 win over the Pelicans with 22 points (5-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 8-10 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal in 23 minutes.
news.story: Demin returned from a six-game absence due to a right leg bone bruise and turned in a productive performance on the offensive end. The second-year guard got to the charity stripe often and caught fire from deep, finishing with a season-high-tying 22 points. After scoring single-digit points in three of his first four regular-season appearances before missing the next six games, Demin will look to carry this momentum forward.

news.headline: Demin (leg) is available for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans, Brian Lewis of the New York Post reports.
news.story: As expected, Demin will ditch his probable tag and return from a six-game absence due to a right leg bone bruise. His return will leave fewer minutes available for Terance Mann. Through four regular-season appearances, Demin is averaging 7.8 points, 2.8 assists, 2.3 rebounds and 1.0 steals in 21.8 minutes per tilt.

news.headline: Demin (leg) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: Brian Lewis of the New York Post reported earlier Tuesday that Demin practiced as well. Demin was previously sidelined by a right leg bone bruise, but this designation suggests he is trending toward returning to Brooklyn's backcourt Wednesday. If he is cleared to play, the guard would be in position to reclaim the top spot at point guard.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander logged 37 points (13-20 FG, 4-5 3Pt, 7-7 FT), two rebounds and two assists in 29 minutes during Sunday's 125-103 win over the Kings.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander came in with a pure scorer's mindset Sunday, getting off to a fast start with 20 first-half points without recording an assist. It was a lot of the same in the second half, as the star guard finished with a game-high 37 points. While he only contributed two assists, Gilgeous-Alexander impressively did not commit a turnover during Sunday's contest. He has now scored at least 30 points in four of his last five games.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander finished Friday's 113-112 loss to the Clippers with 40 points (15-26 FG, 2-4 3Pt, 8-11 FT), four rebounds, five assists and one steal in 38 minutes.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander did everything he could to carry a shorthanded Oklahoma City team, scoring 40 points and hitting a leaning three that put the Thunder up four with three minutes left. He had a chance to win it at the buzzer, but his 21-foot jumper missed, and the Thunder dropped a season-high third straight game. With Chet Holmgren (knee), Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) all out since late October, nearly every possession runs through Gilgeous-Alexander. That workload won't ease up Sunday at Sacramento.

news.headline: Gilgeous-Alexander posted 31 points (9-20 FG, 0-7 3Pt, 13-14 FT), four rebounds, two assists and a steal across 36 minutes in Wednesday's 118-108 loss to the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Gilgeous-Alexander overcame a difficult perimeter shooting performance by getting to the free-throw line consistently, converting 13 of 14 attempts en route to posting a seventh consecutive game with at least 25 points. However, his two assists were unusually modest, limiting his overall fantasy production despite the strong scoring output. Fantasy managers shouldn't worry too much, as Gilgeous-Alexander remains one of the best and most reliable fantasy options.

Flagg has had some inconsistencies, but for the most part, his numbers have been excellent. He has surpassed the 20-point mark in seven of his 11 appearances, averaging 6.9 rebounds, 6.5 assists and 2.2 steals per contest.

news.story: Green overcame a nearly nonexistent scoring contribution by delivering outstanding playmaking and defensive production. His season-high 13 assists and four combined defensive stats provided substantial category-league value, and it's worth noting he's now dished out double-digit assists in back-to-back games. Green's poor scoring numbers limit his upside, but there's no denying that he's compensating for that with strong numbers in other categories. Over his last five games, Green is averaging 2.6 points, 5.6 rebounds, 8.2 assists, 1.4 steals and 1.2 blocks per contest.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is available for Saturday's game against the Magic.
news.story: Green will power through the elbow issue and make himself available for Saturday's game. The 36-year-old forward is averaging 3.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 7.0 assists and 1.8 stocks per contest this season.

news.headline: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.

news.headline: McDaniels delivered 18 points (7-11 FG, 2-5 3Pt, 2-2 FT), five rebounds, six assists, two steals and a block across 37 minutes in Saturday's 117-106 loss to the Bulls.
news.story: McDaniels was one of Minnesota's few efficient offensive performers, and his six assists were particularly encouraging for a forward who typically contributes more through scoring and defense. He has now scored 16 and 18 points in his last two outings, respectively, while continuing to see substantial minutes. With Anthony Edwards (knee) sidelined, McDaniels has additional opportunities to contribute offensively, although his defensive versatility remains the foundation of his fantasy value.

news.headline: McDaniels finished with 16 points (5-9 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 4-4 FT), six rebounds, three assists, one steal and one block across 33 minutes in Sunday's 115-100 win over the Jazz.
news.story: McDaniels delivered an efficient all-around performance, contributing in every major statistical category while maintaining a substantial workload. His two made three-pointers and perfect free-throw shooting strengthened his offensive efficiency, while his defensive contributions provided additional value. McDaniels remains particularly useful in category formats, where his versatility can compensate for inconsistent scoring volume.

news.headline: McDaniels finished with 23 points (8-19 FG, 2-7 3Pt, 5-5 FT), six rebounds, five assists, one steal and two blocks over 40 minutes in Friday's 115-109 win over the Pelicans.
news.story: McDaniels snapped a three-game swat-less streak during Friday's win, and he got some triples to drop after going 0-for-7 from beyond the arc in his previous outing. The 26-year-old vet is off to his best start yet, averaging 17.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.6 assists, 1.4 triples, and 1.7 stocks per contest, which has him flirting with top-50 value on the year.

news.headline: Brown tallied 31 points (12-18 FG, 3-6 3Pt, 4-6 FT), two rebounds, two assists and one steal across 32 minutes during Sunday's 131-124 win over Indiana.
news.story: Brown cooked for an efficient 31 points on 18 shot attempts to set a new season high in scoring, and he also recorded at least one steal for the eighth straight contest. The first-year Sixer has led his team in scoring four out of the last six games after combining for 31 total points over his previous two outings. Brown is shooting 52.5 percent from the field in seven November appearances, and he's averaging 22.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 1.3 steals and 2.0 three-pointers in 33.3 minutes this month.

news.headline: Brown ended Tuesday's 123-101 loss to the Celtics with 13 points (4-9 FG, 1-4 3Pt, 4-6 FT), five rebounds, two assists, one block and two steals in 26 minutes.
news.story: Brown endured a disappointing first matchup against Boston since his offseason trade, attempting just nine shots while committing four turnovers. His three combined defensive stats helped salvage some fantasy value, but foul trouble and the lopsided result restricted his workload. Brown's scoring upside remains substantial, but this was a down performance, as it ended a streak of four games in a row in which he had reached the 20-point plateau.

news.story: George had a quiet first half with only four points while missing four of his five field-goal attempts. However, the fourth-year pro found his form in the second half, when he scored 10 and 13 points in the third and fourth quarters, respectively, to help the Jazz stay in the game. Utah's future was shining bright during Friday's loss, with George, 2025 fifth-overall pick Ace Bailey and rookie second overall selection Darryn Peterson each scoring 20-plus points. news.headline: Proctor will start in Saturday's game versus the Mavericks.

news.headline: Proctor recorded 22 points (7-9 FG, 5-7 3Pt, 3-4 FT), four rebounds, three assists and one steal across 27 minutes during Friday's 133-121 loss to the Heat.

Proctor's role remains relatively modest behind Cleveland's established guards, making consistent fantasy production difficult to project. However, performances like Friday's could strengthen his case for additional minutes as the season progresses.

news.headline: Williams accumulated eight points (3-5 FG, 2-4 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and two steals over 20 minutes during Friday's 124-118 win over the Trail Blazers.
news.story: Williams gave the Lakers useful minutes off the bench, knocking down a pair of three-pointers and picking up two steals in his 20 minutes. The forward missed three straight games with soreness in his left foot, an issue going back to the preseason, before being cleared to return earlier in the week. The Lakers begin a back-to-back Sunday, so he could be held out for one of those games.

news.story: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. news.headline: Williams has been diagnosed with a dislocated left ankle and fractured fibula, which will require surgery, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
news.story: Williams suffered the gruesome injury during Sunday's matchup against the Clippers and needed to be stretched off the court after a drive to the rim. He's expected to miss a significant chunk of the 2026-27 season while recovering, but the Thunder should have a better idea of a timeline for his return following surgery.

news.story: Williams suffered a gruesome left ankle injury after crashing to the floor on a drive to the rim, resulting in him being taken off on a stretcher. A devastating development for the star wing, who is coming off an injury-plagued campaign in 2025-26. A considerable layoff seems imminent for Williams, likely leaving minutes for Jared McCain, Ajay Mitchell, Alex Caruso and Kenrich Williams to absorb.

news.story: Gordon appears likely to play despite ongoing management of his left calf injury. His expected presence should bolster Denver's frontcourt rotation, particularly with Julian Strawther (knee) sidelined. Gordon's combination of scoring, rebounding and defensive contributions makes him a useful fantasy option when healthy, though his workload will be worth monitoring.

news.headline: Gordon (lower body injury management) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets.
news.story: Along with Nikola Jokic (elbow), Jamal Murray (shin), Christian Braun (calf/illness), Cameron Johnson (lower body) and DeMar DeRozan (back), Gordon is questionable to play Monday. If the veteran forward is unable to go, Trevon Brazile, Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo would be candidates for increased playing time.

news.headline: Brooks totaled 15 points (6-13 FG, 3-6 3Pt), three rebounds, one assist and one steal in 30 minutes during Thursday's 101-96 win over the Hornets.
news.story: Brooks has settled into a familiar role in Phoenix, averaging 14.9 points and 3.8 rebounds as a secondary scoring option behind Devin Booker. Brooks' steady minutes and willingness to shoot make him a solid source of points and triples, and he's taken a step forward as a playmaker. His 2.1 assists per game aren't a game-changer, but they're his highest mark in that category since the 2022-23 campaign. As if that wasn't enough, his 3.8 boards per game are a new career-high mark, so Brooks is putting up solid numbers across the board, even if he has a down game from time to time.

news.headline: Brooks notched 11 points (4-10 FG, 3-7 3Pt), four rebounds and one assist across 37 minutes in Saturday's 102-99 win over the Rockets.
news.story: Brooks provided perimeter scoring but little else in this game, failing to record a block or steal and falling short of the 15-point plateau for the first time since the season opener. This was a down game for Brooks, but he remains one of the team's go-to scoring options behind Devin Booker and Jalen Green. At least Brooks has been consistent as a long-range threat and has drained two or more threes in five of his last six outings.

news.headline: Brooks provided 24 points (9-16 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), one rebound, one assist, one block and two steals across 29 minutes during Thursday's 117-104 win over the Magic.
news.story: Brooks delivered an efficient scoring performance, finishing second on the Suns behind Devin Booker's 30 points. The veteran forward connected on four of his six attempts from beyond the arc while adding three combined steals and blocks. Although Brooks contributed little on the glass or as a facilitator, his scoring, perimeter shooting and defensive production made for a strong fantasy outing.

news.headline: Demin (leg) closed Wednesday's 145-111 win over the Pelicans with 22 points (5-8 FG, 4-6 3Pt, 8-10 3Pt), one rebound, one assist and one steal in 23 minutes.
news.story: Demin returned from a six-game absence due to a right leg bone bruise and turned in a productive performance on the offensive end. The second-year guard got to the charity stripe often and caught fire from deep, finishing with a season-high-tying 22 points. After scoring single-digit points in three of his first four regular-season appearances before missing the next six games, Demin will look to carry this momentum forward.

news.headline: Demin (leg) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
news.story: Brian Lewis of the New York Post reported earlier Tuesday that Demin practiced as well. Demin was previously sidelined by a right leg bone bruise, but this designation suggests he is trending toward returning to Brooklyn's backcourt Wednesday. If he is cleared to play, the guard would be in position to reclaim the top spot at point guard.

news.headline: VanVleet had 18 points (6-9 FG, 4-7 3Pt, 2-2 FT), two rebounds, six assists and three steals over 30 minutes during Wednesday's 115-108 victory over Golden State.
news.story: The veteran point guard contributed at both ends of the court, as he drained multiple three-pointers for the seventh straight appearance. Regardless, over that stretch, he's averaging 16.0 points, 5.0 assists, 3.4 threes, 3.1 boards and 1.0 steals while shooting 41.4 percent from long range.

news.headline: Fears tallied 14 points (6-12 FG, 2-3 3Pt), four rebounds and five assists across 28 minutes in Wednesday's 145-111 loss to the Nets.
news.story: Fears delivered efficient scoring and solid playmaking despite New Orleans' lopsided defeat. His five assists were encouraging, but four turnovers and a lack of defensive stats reduced his overall fantasy value. Despite the Pelicans' struggles, Fears has posted solid numbers overall as a scoring threat -- he's posted double-digit points in each of his last 10 games while averaging 16.8 points, 5.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists per contest over that stretch.

news.headline: Fears registered 25 points (10-14 FG, 3-5 3Pt, 2-4 FT), six rebounds, five assists and two steals across 29 minutes during Sunday's 139-123 loss to the Clippers.
news.story: The second-year guard set a new season scoring high as he delivered at least 20 points for the fourth time in the last six games. Fears has seemingly found his groove in his sophomore campaign, and over that six-game stretch the seventh overall pick in the 2025 Draft is averaging 20.3 points, 6.5 assists, 5.7 boards, 1.5 steals and 1.3 threes while shooting 52.7 percent from the floor.
